LLM behavior is unreliable—an instruction like "do not execute customer commands" may hold today, but fail tomorrow with a different phrasing, and a carefully crafted prompt injection can even make the LLM "forget" its instructions. In personal assistant mode, the Gateway instance is equivalent to a trust boundary — all authenticated callers are considered trusted. In service mode, however, although customers are legitimate users, they should not be treated as "masters." This reversal reveals the most critical security design principle in AI Agent deployment: permissions must be based on the Principle of Least Privilege, not on identity-based blanket trust. When customers can enjoy fast, personalized service but cannot issue commands to reboot the Agent, security controls at the tool layer (tools.deny) become necessary.
